Command-Line Reference > sa sla check

sa sla check

sa sla check performs lexical, syntax, and type checking on a .sla source file. After reading this page you can quickly verify that source passes the frontend checks without generating any artifacts.

Transition noteThe host-verb spelling sa check <file.sla> is now preferred; sa sla check still works but prints a deprecation note. The two forms run the same pipeline.

Syntax

usage: sa sla check [file] [-p <package>]

Parameters

NameDescription
fileThe .sla source file to check; when omitted, the sa.mod workspace is resolved upward from the current directory, taking the member entry point src/main.sla (or main.sla).
-p, --packageSelect the member package in workspace mode; supports -p name / -p=name / --package=name.
-h, --helpShow usage and return 0.

Execution stages

check passes through, in order: macro template expansion → parsing (expansion of SLA sources and std contracts from @import) → generic specialization (monomorphize) → contract loading → type checking. If any stage fails, a diagnostic of the corresponding category is printed to stderr and a non-zero status is returned, for example Type Check Error: failed to verify types: ....

Notecheck does not emit final SA assembly, nor does it write SAB; it only verifies that “the frontend can take it in”. Passing the frontend does not mean backend lowering will necessarily succeed — there is a known gap between the two.

Stage-by-stage diagnostics

The stages named above produce distinct diagnostic families. Knowing which family you are looking at tells you which file to edit:

StageTypical failureWhere to look
Macro template expansionan undefined macro or a malformed @expand_tuple / @derivethe macro declaration and its call site
Parse + @import expansionSyntax Error, or Import Error: ... FileNotFoundthe imported path and SA_STD_DIR
Monomorphizea generic instance that cannot be specializedthe generic declaration and its concrete arguments
Contract loadinga missing .sai / .sal contractthe @import target and the project root
Type checkingType Check Error: failed to verify types: ..., e.g. UseAfterMovethe reported source line

Measured success output on the generated skeleton (note that the path is echoed verbatim):

$ sa sla check /tmp/opencode/initdemo/src/main.sla
Sla Compiler: Successfully parsed and verified syntax and types of /tmp/opencode/initdemo/src/main.sla.

check vs build vs build-exe

CommandStops afterOn-disk output
sa sla checktype checkingnone
sa sla buildSA text emission<stem>.sa
sa sla build-exenative linkexecutable

When a program passes check but fails build-exe, the fault is in backend lowering, not in your syntax or types. That split is deliberate: the frontend can accept more than the backend can lower today (see the Feature Maturity Matrix).

Examples

# 显式文件
SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa sla check tests/test_unit_basic.sla

# 在 workspace 成员目录里省略文件参数
cd my_app
SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa sla check

# 从 workspace 根目录指定成员
SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa sla check -p my_app

# Rosetta demo
SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa sla check demos/rosetta/01_hello_world/main.sla

Output and artifact locations

On success, stdout prints one line:

Sla Compiler: Successfully parsed and verified syntax and types of src/main.sla.

There are no on-disk artifacts. check neither reads nor writes .sla-cache/sab/.
